analyst_view.overall: Early view: two of the best defences in the division meet, with Mallorca sixth (7 conceded, five wins from six at home) and Castellón second (5 conceded in 12, the best away record). Both had their round 13 game postponed after Jesús de Miguel's death; Castellón, his former club, asked for theirs to be called off, and Mallorca still have the Andorra game to fit in. Matías Orozco's ban should be served at Valladolid on 14 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals. I lean slightly lower: Castellón have conceded only five goals all season and four away, while Mallorca have let in three at home, so a 1-0 or 1-1 type of game looks most likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. I found nothing that points either way on corners for these two, so I stay with the site's number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. Mallorca are card-prone (36 yellows and a red in 12 games) and Castellón coach Pablo Hernández was furious with the referee after Orozco's red at Burgos, but the site's number already reflects a busy game for the referee.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.1 shots. Both teams can control games, Castellón with their 4-0 over Sporting and Mallorca at home, so a total in the mid 20s fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. I lean lower: both defences limit clear chances, and Castellón in particular rarely let opponents get shots on goal.
